identify.intro: Europa trucks were certified for the US when new, which is what separates them from gray-market Gs imported later. Paperwork and the VIN do most of the work.

items.head: VIN format
items.body: Bring a Trailer's 2000–2001 Europa G 500s carry 17-character US-format VINs beginning WDBEG42, with the 10th character as the model-year code (Y = 2000, 1 = 2001). The 1998 Europa G 320s listed there show VINs in the European style, beginning WDB463231 (W463 model code). Neither decodes fully in NHTSA's vPIC tool, so lean on paperwork as well.

items.head: Compliance label and invoices
items.body: A real Europa truck has a federal compliance label and Europa sales paperwork, not a foreign VIN cleared later by an independent lab. Match the VIN on the label, the chassis and the invoices.

items.head: Recall records
items.body: Europa filed its own NHTSA recalls under the make 'EUROPA' (e.g. 01V064, covering 1992–2001 trucks). A completed Europa recall in the service file is good evidence of a factory-certified truck.

items.head: G 320 engine
items.body: 1998 was the changeover year, so a G 320 can have the M104 inline-six or the M112 V6. Read the engine code rather than trusting the model year.

items.head: Europa versus 2002 MBUSA G 500
items.body: A Europa G 500 has black-painted bumpers, the pre-facelift W210 E-Class steering wheel and cluster, no wheel-mounted radio buttons, older climate controls and a 722.6 automatic without the tip-shift gate.

values.intro: Prices are broad because BaT lumps Europa trucks in with gray-market W463s. Short-wheelbase and Cabriolet versions sell for far more than five-door wagons.
values.note: Based on 33 Bring a Trailer sales of 1993–2001 petrol W463 wagons, SWBs and Cabriolets from January 2025 to October 2026, nine of them titled 'Europa'. The Europa-titled sales ran from $19,250 (2001 G 500) to $114,000 (2000 G 500 SWB), and a 2000 G 500 Cabriolet Europa made $230,000.

paragraphs: A Europa G doesn't need to be imported: Europa International certified these trucks to US safety and emissions standards when they were new. That's the difference from gray-market W463s brought in privately, one at a time, and it's why Europa paperwork matters when you buy.

NHTSA lets a vehicle that is at least 25 years old be imported without meeting the FMVSS, counting from its date of manufacture. That now covers every 1990s W463, so European-market versions Europa never sold can come in legally. That's one reason so many 1990s Gs on the US market today were never Europa trucks. Check state titling and emissions rules before buying one.
